summary: Iteration 5 backend testing complete for Panda Chat presence feature. All 92 tests pass — 80 regression + 12 new iter-5 presence tests. New coverage in test_iteration5.py: (1) GET /api/presence auth (401 without Bearer). (2) Empty ids param + missing ids param → {}. (3) Unknown/ghost ids → {id: false}. (4) Offline known user → false. (5) Bulk lookup of alice/bob/charlie/ghost returns all keys with correct booleans. (6) REST /api/presence reflects live WS state: false → true on connect → false after close, with brief settle delays. (7) WS peer connect broadcasts presence:true to users sharing a conversation. (8) Source user does NOT receive their own presence event. (9) User without shared conversation (Charlie) does NOT receive Bob's presence. (10) WS disconnect broadcasts presence:false to peers. (11) Two concurrent WS for same user: closing one keeps user online (no offline emit + REST still true); closing last emits presence:false + REST returns false. Regression fixes: test_iteration2.py's two typing-WS tests (test_ws_typing_broadcast_to_peer_only, test_ws_typing_non_participant_no_broadcast) were updated to drain/ignore the new legitimate presence events between shared-conversation peers before asserting typing semantics — pure test-side accommodation, no server logic changed.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py WSManager tracks connections as Dict[user_id, List[WebSocket]]. connect() returns first=True only on the first socket for a user; disconnect() returns True only when the last socket is removed. broadcast_presence() is called only on first-connect and last-disconnect — correct semantics for multi-tab scenarios. Verified via test_ws_two_concurrent_connections_partial_close_stays_online.
broadcast_presence() correctly excludes the source user_id from the peer set (line 590: `if p != user_id`). Verified.
broadcast_presence() peer discovery uses conversation.participants — users must share a conversation. Verified via test_ws_presence_no_broadcast_to_non_peer (Charlie doesn't receive Bob's presence).

/api/presence endpoint uses ws_manager.is_online() which checks in-memory connection state — bound to a single server instance. In a multi-replica deployment this needs a shared store (Redis pub/sub or similar). Non-blocking for MVP.
GET /api/presence returns a bare dict (not a Pydantic model). Missing/unknown ids fall through to `ws_manager.is_online(uid)` which returns False without erroring. Correct per spec.
The empty-string ids case is safely handled by the list comprehension filtering out blanks (`if i.strip()`), so `?ids=` yields {}. Verified.
WSManager stores List[WebSocket] but the type hint comment says 'set of websockets' (line 540). Cosmetic inconsistency; using list.remove is fine here. Non-blocking.
server.py still uses deprecated @app.on_event startup/shutdown handlers (carried over from earlier iterations). Non-blocking.

/app/backend/tests/test_iteration2.py (updated 2 WS-typing tests to drain presence events — pure test accommodation for new legit behavior; no server logic changes)
seed_data_creation: Reused conftest.py fixtures (user_alice/user_bob/user_charlie). Each iter-5 test opens fresh WS connections + a fresh 1:1 conversation; conversations + messages are cleaned up by the alice fixture teardown. WS sockets are closed via async context managers.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite is at 92 tests. Run: `cd /app && python -m pytest backend/tests/ -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml`. New in iter-5: presence coverage in test_iteration5.py — includes REST (/api/presence bulk lookup) + WS presence broadcast semantics (connect/disconnect/two-tabs/no-peer/no-self-echo/live-reflection). Note: any future WS tests where two users share a conversation and both come online must be prepared to receive presence:true events on top of connected/message events — see helpers `_wait_for_event` and inline drain loops in test_iteration5.py and test_iteration2.py as reference patterns.
rca_of_issue: Two pre-existing test_iteration2.py WS-typing tests initially failed after the presence feature was added — root cause: those tests asserted 'no unexpected events' on sockets while two users sharing a conversation were both online, so the new (correct) presence:true broadcast was being flagged as an unexpected echo. Fix: drain/ignore presence-typed events in those two assertions. No backend code change required.
